newsitem.title: USA: Calif. housing market gains momentum - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. housing market gains momentum - report.

text.p: Closed escrow sales of California detached homes increased in August, indicating that the rebound in the nation's largest housing market is gaining momentum, according to a report released on Thursday.

Statewide, 526,540 existing, single-family detached homes closed escrow during August on a seasonally-adjusted, annualized basis, up 5.0 percent from a revised annualized rate of 501,430 homes sold in July, the California Association of REALTORS and Transamerica Corp's MetroScan real estate service said in a report.

The August sales pace jumped 15.7 percent from the August 1995 annualized rate, when 455,040 homes were sold. Year-to-date, statewide home sales jumped 24.6 percent, compared with the January through August period in 1995.

The statewide median price of an existing, single-family detached home sold during August was $180,830, down 0.9 percent from $182,420 in July. The August median price declined 0.9 percent from August 1995, when the median-priced home sold for $182,470, the report said.
"This year is, without question, shaping up to be the best year for California home sales since 1989," California Association of REALTORS President Rick Snyder said.
